_meta.description: PBO EFO Sept 2025 vs DoF SEU April 2026 five-year deficit projections.

_meta.units: billions CAD, federal government total budgetary balance (negative = deficit)
_meta.methodology_note: PBO EFO uses PBO staff macro projection (status-quo policy assumption); DoF SEU uses private-sector survey vintage Aug 2025 plus Budget 2025 measures. Vintage gap: PBO Sept 25 2025, DoF April 28 2026. Delta is partly methodology, partly forecast vintage. PBO's medium-term path 2026-27 through 2029-30 is published in the EFO PDF as a year-by-year table but only the anchor years (2024-25 and 2025-26) are press-accessible; the PBO press release characterises the middle years as 'close to $60 billion' through the medium term. The chart shows verified anchor values and uses the PBO's own 'close to $60bn' framing for the middle years rather than fabricating a year-specific path.
_meta.pbo_vintage: PBO Economic and Fiscal Outlook, September 2025 (RP-2526-012-S, released 2025-09-25)
_meta.dof_vintage: Department of Finance Canada, Spring Economic Update 2026 (released 2026-04-28)
_meta.next_update: PBO EFO next: fall 2026; DoF: Budget 2026 (timing TBD)

pbo_efo_sept_2025.notes: PBO EFO Sept 2025 (RP-2526-012-S, released 2025-09-25) verified: 2024-25 $51.7bn (1.7% GDP); 2025-26 $68.5bn (2.2% GDP); medium-term (2026-27 through 2029-30) framed as 'close to $60 billion through the medium term' in the PBO press release. The middle-year placeholder of -$60.0bn is the PBO's own anchor framing rendered as a band, not a year-specific forecast. Chart caption should treat the 2026-27 through 2029-30 segment as 'PBO horizon: ~$60bn' rather than as four distinct year-specific points.
